case_name: Devilal Modi, Proprietor, Messrs Daluram Pannalal Modi v Sales Tax Officer, Ratlam and Others
petitioner: Devilal Modi, Proprietor, Messrs Daluram Pannalal Modi
facts: The appellant, Devilal Modi, is the Proprietor of M/s. Daluram Pannalal Modi and has been assessed to sales-tax for the year 1957-58 under the Madhya Bharat Sales Tax Act, 1950.
He challenged the validity of the said order of assessment by a writ petition filed by him (No. 114/1961) in the High Court of Madhya Pradesh on the 25th April, 1961.
The High Court dismissed his writ petition and by special leave, the appellant came to this Court in appeal against the said decision of the High Court.
On the 8th March, 1963, the appellant's appeal by special leave was dismissed by this Court.
Thereafter, the appellant filed the present writ petition in the same High Court on the 23rd April, 1963 (No. 129/1963).
By this writ petition the appellant challenges the validity of the same order of assessment.
issues: Whether the principle of constructive res judicata can be invoked against a writ petition filed by the appellant Devilal Modi?
Is it permissible to the appellant to attack the validity of the same order imposing a sales-tax and penalty on him for the year 1957-58 by two consecutive writ petitions?
petitioner_arguments: The principle of constructive res judicata is not applicable to writ proceedings.

A citizen should be allowed to challenge the validity of the same order by successive petitions under Art. 226, as long as a case is made out for the exercise of jurisdiction in support of a citizen's fundamental rights.
respondent_arguments: The principle of constructive res judicata is applicable to writ proceedings and should be invoked against the appellant Devilal Modi.
A party should not be allowed to take one proceeding after another and urge new grounds every time, as it would be open to the party to do so.
court_reasoning: The general principle underlying the doctrine of res judicata is ultimately based on considerations of public policy.
One important consideration of public policy is that the decisions pronounced by courts of competent jurisdiction should be final, unless they are modified or reversed by appellate authorities.
Another principle is that no one should be made to face the same kind of litigation twice over, because such a process would be contrary to considerations of fair play and justice.
holding: The Court holds that the principle of constructive res judicata is applicable to writ proceedings and should be invoked against the appellant Devilal Modi.
A party should not be allowed to take one proceeding after another and urge new grounds every time, as it would be open to the party to do so.
